tagline: Auto mode's classifier reads **only the agent's message text** — so an approval you typed in chat is **invisible** to it.
summary: When auto (or background) mode decides whether an action is safe to take unattended, a **classifier** makes the call — and it reads a **narrow input**: the agent's own **message text**. It does **not** read tool output, subagent reports, or your **AskUserQuestion answers**. The consequence catches people: you can approve something in the conversation and the classifier **still blocks it**, because the approval never lived in the one channel it reads. The fix is to route the grant through your own authority — a **`!`-prefixed command** — rather than retrying the tool call.

sections.heading: A narrow window
body: Auto mode runs without per-action consent (it **no longer requires opt-in**). To stay safe it leans on a **classifier** that judges each action. The non-obvious part is **what the classifier can see**: the agent's **message text**, and that's the load-bearing input.

It does **not** ingest tool results, the reports a subagent hands back, or the answers you pick in an **AskUserQuestion** prompt. Those are real and they happened — they're just **outside the classifier's window**.

sections.heading: Why your approval doesn't land
body: When you confirm a sensitive operation in conversation — "yes, edit the ACL", "go ahead, log in" — that consent lives in the **dialogue**, not in the agent's next message text in a form the classifier recognizes as authorization. So the classifier, reading only the message text, **never sees the approval** and keeps **blocking** the grant.

This is why production grants (ACL edits, logins, vault scans, self-modifying config) can be blocked **repeatedly even after you've said yes**. The retry loops because each retry presents the classifier the same window — and the approval still isn't in it.

sections.heading: Route around it, don't fight it
body: The working move is to stop feeding the classifier and use **your own authority**: run the blocked grant via a **`!`-prefixed in-session command**, which executes as **you**, not as a tool call the classifier must clear.

Read this as a **boundary**, not a bug: the classifier is intentionally conservative about a small input rather than trusting a chat transcript it can't fully verify. Knowing its window tells you where to apply the override.

diagram.caption: The classifier reads **only the agent's message text**. Approvals in other channels never reach it — so route the grant through your own `!` command.

nodes.label: Agent's message text
nodes.note: The **only** input the classifier reads. Whatever the agent says here is what gets judged.

nodes.label: Tool output · subagent reports · AskUserQuestion answers
nodes.note: All real, all present in the session — and all **outside the classifier's window**. Your in-chat approval lives here, where the classifier can't see it.

nodes.label: Safety classifier
nodes.note: Judges the action from the **message text alone**. It cannot consult the channels where your approval actually lives.

nodes.label: Safe to do unattended?
nodes.note: Routine actions pass. A **sensitive grant** (ACL edit, login, vault scan, self-config) fails — the approval that would clear it was never in the window.

nodes.label: Grant blocked — repeatedly
nodes.note: Retrying the tool call presents the **same window**, so it blocks again. The loop isn't stubbornness; the approval simply isn't an input.

nodes.label: Route via `!`-prefixed command
nodes.note: Run the grant under **your** authority with a `!` command instead of a tool call. It executes as you — bypassing the classifier's narrow window entirely.

scenarios.title: A grant is **blocked despite a yes** in chat
scenarios.note: The classifier judged the message text, found a sensitive grant, and blocked — the approval you typed was never an input to the decision.

scenarios.title: Why the approval is invisible — and how to route around it
scenarios.note: Your consent lived in AskUserQuestion answers / dialogue — outside the window. Stop retrying the tool call; run the grant via a `!` command.

misconceptions.myth: If I approve the action in chat, auto mode will proceed.
misconceptions.reality: The classifier reads **only the agent's message text**. Your in-conversation approval lives in channels it doesn't read, so the grant keeps getting blocked.
misconceptions.why: We assume anything said in the session is "in context" for every decision. The classifier's input is deliberately narrower than the conversation.

misconceptions.myth: The classifier weighs tool output and subagent reports when judging safety.
misconceptions.reality: It reads neither — nor AskUserQuestion answers. Only the agent's message text feeds the decision.
misconceptions.why: A rich session feels like a shared context. But the classifier is a small, conservative gate over one input, not a reader of the whole transcript.

misconceptions.myth: Auto mode pauses to ask for consent before sensitive operations.
misconceptions.reality: Auto mode **no longer requires opt-in consent**; a classifier gates actions instead — and because it reads only message text, sensitive grants are best routed through a `!`-prefixed command.
misconceptions.why: Earlier autonomy was consent-gated, so the habit lingers. Now the gate is a classifier, and the override point moved with it.
